abstract: Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-filled epoxy resin has been widely used as basic materials for insulators in ac/dc power transmission applications. Under normal working condition, charges injection from electrodes accelerates the dielectric aging rate and distorts the surface electric field, which is followed by dielectric degradation and breakdown. Therefore, to restrain the charge injection is of very important significance, especially when the dielectric was operating under temperature gradients. In this paper, to regulate the charge injection of dielectrics under temperature gradient, Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> coatings composed of dense well organized Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> molecules were created on the insulation surface. The surface potential appears low increments for modified samples, which indicates less charge injection phenomenon. Only slight surface potential increment was found using samples modified by Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> coating with thickness of 1000 nm, even when the temperature of HV electrode reaching 100 °C. Therefore, we believe that the Cr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> coating can effectively suppress the charge injection from the electrode, which has excellent application significance.

articleTitle: Experimental study of dielectric properties of fumed silica/silicone composites
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubbers are widely used polymer materials, particularly in high voltage insulation applications for their superior electrical, thermal, and chemical properties compared to other commonly used polymers. In industry, silicone elastomers are heavily filled with fumed silica particles in order to obtain superior mechanical properties. For a better understanding of the interaction between the silicon dioxide nano particles (fumed silica) and silicone rubber matrix as well as the dielectric properties of fumed silica/silicone composites, dielectric spectroscopy measurements were carried out over a wide frequency range from near DC up to 2MHz. Silicone rubber composite samples filled with surface treated fumed silica particles were prepared by hot pressing and the effects of filler concentration, filler surface treatment, and mixing method on the dielectric properties are investigated. The effect of filler-polymer interaction has been analyzed by comparing the dielectric spectroscopy measurement data with scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images.

articleTitle: Motion and discharge behavior of the free conducting linear particle within DC GIL
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: To investigate the motion and discharge behavior of free conducting linear particles in DC GIL, a coaxial cylindrical electrode is set up, with a high-speed camera to observe the motion and air-gap breakdown of the particles. The research work studies the charging behavior of the particle under DC voltage, then analyzes the particle's lifting voltage theoretically and experimentally. Two different motion patterns are observed, e.g. standing and bouncing, and the relationship between the probabilities of the two states' occurrence and the length of the particle is investigated through experiments. Mechanical analysis of the air-gap breakdown caused by free conducting linear particle is conducted based on the stream theory. The experimental results indicate that the lifting voltage of the linear particle is almost irrelevant to the length of the particle but has strong correlation with the radius. The length of the particle has an impact on the motion patterns, i.e. the shorter the particle, the greater the probability of bouncing, and vice versa. The length of micro-discharge gap increases with the particle length, while the breakdown voltage decreases with the particle length.

articleTitle: Economic application of powder resin based groundwall insulation for low voltage electric drives
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Powder coating already forms an established variant of groundwall insulation although being used almost exclusively for small, flyer-wound rotors mostly due to the lack of economic application and curing processes for larger drives. However, insulation layers based on powder coatings are able to perform significantly better than common aramid-based slot liners. Regarding recent developments in powder application and curing, efficient application methods regarding energy consumption and process time are able to increase yield significantly. Regarding the altering topological characteristics of modern traction drives e.g. for electric vehicles, powder application and achievable results have to be investigated to assess the value of an industrial implementation. Experiments were performed using an electrostatic coating cell and a fixture simulating various characteristics of modern drives including inner diameter, slot width and -depth. These characteristics as well as available process values were analyzed towards the target figure coating thickness using DoE methods. Results predict a valid application of electrostatic powder coating within certain limits for larger traction drives. Package length should not exceed 80 mm and the diameter to package-length ratio has to be lower than 1.0 in order to achieve consistent, repeatable results. Electrostatic Powder Coating can be a valid alternative regarding groundwall insulation for traction drives, although the regarded process is expected to be best-suited for hybrid applications, due to large diameters and small package lengths of electric drives in this field.

articleTitle: Equivalent salt deposit density prediction of outdoor polymer insulators during salt fog test
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Contamination flashover happens when soluble or non-soluble deposits cover the surface of the insulator which results in a reduction in its surface resistance. Many researchers used the leakage current to predict the contamination level on the surface of ceramic outdoor insulators. This can be used as a mean to warn transmission power operators about the advent of contamination flashover. However, there have been few researches to predict the contamination levels on the surface of non-composite or polymer insulators. This work aims to develop a practical technique to monitor and evaluate the surface condition of non-composite by predicting the soluble contamination level known as equivalent salt deposit density (ESDD).

articleTitle: Space charge properties of LDPE-based composites with three types of POSS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polyethylene has been widely used as the insulation material in power cables. POSS (Polyhedral Oligomeric SilSesquioxanes) is a type of filler that may improve the properties of polyethylene. In this paper, space charge characteristics of low density polyethylene (LDPE) based composites containing three different unreactive POSS have been studied. The three unreactive POSS are OmPOSS (OctaMethyl POSS), OibPOSS (OctalsoButyl POSS) and IoPOSS (IsoOctyl POSS). It has been found that the charge injection threshold field of neat LDPE is higher than that of three POSS composites. The different charge dynamics under higher applied voltage in the neat LDPE and three POSS composites show that the charge mobility, trap density, trap depth, recombination between opposite sign of charge are different. This helps us to understand how the structure of POSS affect polymer properties.

articleTitle: Numerical simulations of sediment deposition on grading electrodes in cooling water dielectric of HVDC converter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The platinum pin-type electrodes are installed in inner water cooling circuits of HVDC converter valves to grade the electrical potential distribution and to protect metal components from electrolytic corrosion. In practice, the inorganic particles such as aluminum compounds in cooling water dielectric would be transported to the surfaces of pin-type grading electrodes and aggregate the inorganic sediment. The previous researches showed the thickness of deposited sediment depended on the electric current density through the surface of grading electrode. In this paper, a mechanism of electrophoretic deposition was proposed to clarify the inorganic sediment deposition on the pin-type grading electrode surfaces. The transport and aggregate processes of charged inorganic particles were simulated by COMSOL software. Based on the calculations of the electric and fluid fields along the grading electrodes in a ±500 kV converter valve, the effects of the electrode current and electrode size on the electrophoretic depositions were analyzed. The calculated and analyzed results indicate that the maximum electric field near the surface of a single-pin electrode tip is much higher than that of a combined triple-pin electrode. Under the electric field, the charged particles in water dielectric near the plastic tube wall with a lower fluid velocity will be expediently transported to the grading electrodes, and aggregate on the electrode surface. The thickness of accumulated or deposited sediment during first 50 days is half of that in duration of 180 days. The transport trajectories of charged particles around the grading electrodes were also obtained. The rate of sediment deposition on the electrodes is dependent mainly on the local current density and the sediment properties, and rarely on the charges of the inorganic particles under a critical value. The rate of sediment deposition would decrease with increasing of sediment thickness due to the high insulation resistance of sediment.

articleTitle: DC partial discharge and flashover characteristics and charging activity on solid insulator in air
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: DC partial discharge (PD) characteristics with PD inception voltage and PD activities are measured depending on the different electrode gap lengths and electrode configurations, and with and without solid insulators as PMMA. The charges deposited on solid insulators are measured by surface potential measurement systems. In this paper, it was concluded that the DC-PD inception and flashover voltages are quantitatively determined by the DC applied electric field and PD space charges and deposited surface charge distributions, depending on the positive and negative DC polarity of applied voltages.

articleTitle: Arc discharge detection caused by short-circuit in AC power supply cord
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Unintentional arc discharge caused by short-circuit of element conductors in power supply cords with electrically and/or mechanically damaged electrical insulation can lead to fire accidents. It is difficult to detect this type of short-circuit with a conventional circuit breaker installed in a distribution panel, because the duration of arc discharge is rather short and the magnitude of the short-circuit current is smaller than the threshold value required for operation of the breaker. A hazard prevention system is strongly required in residential areas and plants. This paper proposes a promising detection method of this kind of arc discharge based on features extracted from a series of laboratory experiments, which characterize the distortion of voltage waveform at the time of arc discharge.

articleTitle: Measurement of space charge accumulation in Dicyclopentadiene resin film at high temperature under high DC stress
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Recently, it is required for electronic device that an insulating material which shows an excellent characteristic at high temperature under high DC stress. In this study, we focused on insulating properties of Dicyclopentadiene (DCP) resin. The DCP resin shows a good thermal property and it is expected to be used as a molded insulating material alternative to the epoxy resin because of its superior moldability with low viscosity. On the other hand, polymer insulation material has a possibility of dielectric breakdown by accumulating of a space charge under a high DC stress. So, we investigated the space charge accumulation behavior in the DCP resin at high temperature under high DC stress using the PEA (Pulsed Electro-Acoustic) method.

articleTitle: Firefly and Standing Still phenomena of free conducting wire-type particles in SF6 under DC voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Compared to spherical particles, which are the most prevalent subjects studied by other researchers, free wire-type metallic particles have unique motion phenomena in electric fields under DC voltage, playing an important role in insulation flaw detection of power equipment. However, this is rarely researched sufficiently. Thus, the enclosed experimental chamber and the observation systems are specially designed and motion characteristics of the wire-type particles, with diameters 0.25 mm, 0.4 mm, 0.65 mm and lengths 1 mm, 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm, are studied. The results show that probabilities of Firefly and Standing Phenomena increase with lengths of wire-type particles increasing, and the phenomena are more likely to appear on the negative electrode. When the pressure decreases and radiuses of particles fall, probabilities of Firefly and Standing Phenomena increase. In the case of 1mm diameter, there are not any special phenomena under various conditions and the motion of particles is disorder. Lastly, the explanation of experimental phenomena is done in the view of space charge.

articleTitle: Comparison of sensor detection sensitivity in Repetitive Partial Discharge Inception Voltage measurement for twisted pair placed in stator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: RPDIV (Repetitive Partial Discharge Inception Voltage) measurement becomes essential to fulfill a certificate test according to IEC60034-18-41IS for inverter-fed motor. In measurement of RPDIV, electromagnetic antenna is often used as a PD sensor. Thus, the detection sensitivity of the sensor is crucial to properly determine RPDIV. This paper deals with sensitivity comparison between kinds of electromagnetic sensors and a PD measuring device connected to a measurement circuit for RPDIV measurement of twisted pair placed in stator.

articleTitle: Modeling the isothermal charge decay of modified polytetrafluoroethylene electrets from their thermally stimulated discharge
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the present paper, we investigate the possibility of using the trap parameters obtained via thermally stimulated discharge to model the isothermal charge decay at different temperatures on polytetrafluoroethylene films treated with titanium-tetrachloride vapor. The energy spectra were extracted from the thermally stimulated surface-potential-decay data obtained for both non-treated and modified films. Using a model based on a theory by Simmons, we model the isothermal charge decay in these electrets and compare it with experimental results. It has been shown that at elevated temperatures there is a reasonably good agreement between modelled and experimental curves, whereas at room temperature there is a considerable discrepancy between both. As at room temperature the electrets tend to discharge faster than predicted, we believe that this indicates the presence of yet another discharge mechanism unaccounted for in theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Detection of shell coatings from core-shell like dielectric nanoparticles with electrostatic force microscopy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Materials in the form of a superposition of thin dielectric layers with nanometric dimensions such as core-shell nanoparticles are used in different nanotechnology fields. Reliable methods are needed to characterize such systems at the nanoscale. In this work, we study the possibility of the electrostatic force microscope (EFM) in the DC force gradient detection method to detect alumina thin layers deposited on polystyrene nanoparticles and on silicon dioxide nanospheres. The dielectric permittivity of these materials is used as their fingerprint. We find that the EFM is sensitive to the thickness of a dielectric layer over studied nanoparticles and over bare substrates.

articleTitle: The effect of annealing temperature on the corrosion behavior of copper in insulating oil contained corrosion sulfur
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Copper corrosion in transformers is one of the serious problems affecting the life of the transformers. Much work has been done to improve corrosion resistant of copper. Grain boundary engineering (GBE) is an effective method to enhance the property of corrosion resistant by optimization of deformation and heat treatment processes to change the number and distribution of the special grain boundary, thus improving material certain macro performance associated with grain boundaries. In this study, pure copper first cold rolled 35%, then annealed at varied temperature. Then, the evolution of grain sizes and special grain boundaries after the processing and annealing have been particularly analyzed by electron back-scatter diffraction (EBSD). Meanwhile, according to IEC62535 standard, the copper samples with two layers insulating paper were immersed in corrosive oil for 72 hours at 150°C. The corrosion of copper samples was investigated. It shows that annealing temperature affects seriously the number of special grain boundary and the grain size of copper sequentially enhancing the corrosion resistant of copper in insulating oil contained corrosion sulfur.

articleTitle: Study on ageing characteristics of insulating pressboard impregnated by mineral-vegetable oil
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Mineral oil is an excellent dielectric liquid with high coolant capability and low cost, playing important roles as both insulators and coolant liquid in oil-immersed power transformer. However, its flash point is too low, and it is poorly biodegradable once the oil spills or leakage occurs. In this work, pressboards impregnated by mixed oil containing pure mineral oil (80 vol%) and vegetable oil (20 vol%) are prepared, and their thermal ageing characteristics are studied. It was found that the degree of polymerization (DP) of the mixed-oil pressboard sample A was decreased more slowly than that of the pure mineral oil-pressboard sample B with the aging time. Dielectric properties of the samples were measured in the frequency range 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> Hz-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Hz. It was found that the dielectric loss tanδ of sample A increased more slowly than that of sample B with the thermal ageing. The breakdown field of the two samples keeps at nearly the same level in the thermal ageing process. It was believed that the mixture oil-pressboard insulation may be a potential alternative to the traditional mineral oil-pressboard insulation used in the power transformer.

articleTitle: Fabrication and dielectric properties of highly loaded polypropylene micro- and nano-composites
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Composites of polypropylene (PP) containing between 50 and 80 wt% of hexagonal Boron Nitride (hBN) were prepared by planetary milling. The additive was both nanometric and micrometric. Samples containing a mix of half nanoparticles and half microparticles were also fabricated in order to test the possible allying of micro and nanocomposites properties. Highly loaded PP showed much higher dielectric losses, especially when filled with micrometric hBN, and consequently a higher dielectric constant. The breakdown strength was maintained at similar values than the neat polymer up to 70 wt% and then was found to decrease significantly. The thermal conductivity was only noticeably higher than the one of neat PP but did not seem to be strongly affected by a variation of concentration from 50 to 80 %. Thermo Gravimetric Analysis was conducted to study the possible contamination during fabrication.

articleTitle: Influence of surface modifications with orthophosphoric acid on the charge stability of polypropylene electrets
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: It is known that both, physico-chemical surface modification and thermal treatment, can lead to enhanced electret properties of dielectric polymers. To further investigate the influence of surface modifications on charge storage in polypropylene (PP) electrets, a combined thermal and chemical treatment with orthophosphoric acid (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>) is applied to PP films. Charged samples are then studied by means of thermally-stimulated-discharge (TSD) experiments, contact-angle measurements and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. From the results, it can be concluded that additional deeper traps have been formed along with the treatment-induced conformation variations on the surface of the PP films. The new traps significantly improve the surface charge-stability of PP electrets.

articleTitle: A versatile model for estimating breakdown voltage and its application for cryogenic gas mixtures
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: An improved model for the estimation of the breakdown voltages of gas mixtures is developed. The application and utility of the model is demonstrated by using it in estimating the breakdown voltages of gas mixtures containing helium and hydrogen that are being developed as an alternative cryogenic insulation and cooling media for certain high temperature superconducting (HTS) power devices. The concept of the developed model, which incorporates a generalization factor m, is presented. The first step of the model performs a nonlinear least square regression on the generalized formula of the pressure normalized ionization coefficient α/p for the parameter approximation. The second step introduces the parameter m that minimizes the root mean square error (RMSE) of the nonlinear least square regression to derive the versatile model. The validity of the model is demonstrated by comparing its estimated values with the results of the experimental breakdown measurements of several gas mixtures. Compared to the conventional breakdown voltage models, the new model showed improved agreement with the experimental results of the breakdown voltages.

articleTitle: Influence of humidity on spectrum characteristics of audible noise of DC transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In order to investigate the influence of humidity on the A-weighting sound pressure values and spectrum characteristics of the audible noise, a laboratory scale corona cage made by stainless steel and a closed environment test chamber made by polymethyl methacrylate box have been constructed. The aluminum conductor steel reinforced (ACSR), which type is JL/G3A-1000/45 and the same as the conductors applied in ± 800kV DC transmission lines, is used and the ultraviolet detection imager is employed to indicate the intensity of the corona discharge in the experiment, which visualized ultra violet signals of the corona discharge. The results reveal that the A-weighting sound pressure level of audible noise increases with the increase of the humidity. With humidity increases from 9.2 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to 25.8 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, the value of A-weighting sound pressure values increases in the corona cage. The humidity affects the spectral components (>100Hz) more pronounced than low spectral components. The low frequency components are mainly the background noise, which construct the low frequency of audible noise. The correlations between the relative humidity and the spectrum of audible noise pave the way for the restriction the value of audible noise to a more reasonable degree for the surrounding area of lines in future.

articleTitle: PD characteristics at square shaped voltages applying two different detecting techniques
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Nowadays power electronic converters are widely used and the fast switching voltage fronts results in an increased stress on the insulation material and may cause a reduction of the HV systems reliability. Nonsinusoidal voltage waveform have influence on the partial discharges (PD) characteristics in insulating systems due to the increased harmonic content which causes problems mainly in electrical PD measurement setups. In fact, impulse voltages cause strong switching disturbances, which make it much more difficult to distinguish PD signals from noise. This work investigates the influence of repetitive steep pulses on different types of test objects exposed to square wave voltages applying two measurement systems each based on different detection principles, the first one based on a resonant PD decoupler and the second one on an antenna sensor with a flat frequency response and the challenges involved. Results reveal an influence of the rise time was observed with both systems however different information were available dependent on the principle used and the PD characteristic versus noise and remnants of the applied voltage.

articleTitle: The influence of oil-impregnated insulation paper's thickness on electrical breakdown strength
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The oil-impregnated insulation paper (OIIP) is widely used in oil-impregnated high voltage apparatuses. The thickness is an important parameter which affects its electrical breakdown strength. This paper presents an experiment research on the influence of OIIP's thickness on breakdown strength under AC, DC and pulsating DC voltages. The short time breakdown experiments were executed and the Weibull distribution was used to process the results. The results show that the breakdown strength of OIIPs was significantly influenced by thickness and voltage waveform. The breakdown strengths of OIIPs with same thickness under DC and pulsating DC voltage are much larger than that under AC voltage. The breakdown strengths of OIIPs decrease with the increasing thickness under AC voltage, while the breakdown strengths increase with the increasing thickness under DC voltage. The breakdown strengths slightly increase with the increasing thickness of OIIPs under pulsating DC voltage (R=1) and pulsating DC voltage (R=1/3). The equivalent series model of OIIP was used to interpret the results, and the thickness of OIIPs influenced the electrical breakdown strength mainly through oil absorption rate.

articleTitle: Observation and modelling of vapor bubble and streamer initiation in water under long duration impulses
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The inception of vapor bubbles and discharges in water under high voltage impulses of long duration (500 μs) is investigated experimentally, and by numerical simulation. Time delay to bubble and discharge inception are measured versus conductivity and voltage, using fast visualization and optical detection with a laser light diffusion system. A decrease of gap resistance versus time is first observed, and attributed to the heating of water due to Joule dissipation. With fixed conductivity and variable voltage, bubble inception is correlated to a nearly constant value of resistance, suggesting that a constant value of temperature is present when bubbles appear. This hypothesis is checked by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: The rustle of electrical trees
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: A laboratory experiment was set out to detect acoustic signals associated with electrical treeing.. Strong acoustic emission in the 10-15 kHz range is present in initial stages of electrical tree development. Appearance and growth of tree branches coincides with diminishing intensity as well as reduced repetition rate of the sound bursts. During the more advanced stages of electrical tree evolution, until the breakdown point, the sound becomes undetectable. These observations are important if acoustic methods were to be used for condition monitoring of insulation with solid dielectrics, such as in high voltage cable systems.

articleTitle: Electric circuit model for simulating ferroelectrets with open-tubular channels
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Equivalent electric circuits are regularly employed in piezoelectric system modeling to study and evaluate electromechanical behaviors. For instance, electric circuit models have been developed to simulate piezoelectricity in lead zirconate titanate ceramics (PZT) and polyvinylidene difluoride films (PVDF). In this contribution, an equivalent electric circuit is presented to simulate the electromechanical behavior of ferroelectrets with open tubular channels. The electric circuit parameters were obtained from experimental measurements and simulation was carried out with Pspice. The results were compared with a previous model developed to simulate curved PVDF transducers and significant improvement at lower frequencies was observed with the proposed model.

articleTitle: Thermal properties of mineral oil admixed with C60 and TiO2 nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Work on modification of insulating liquids with different nanoparticles to improve their electric properties has been done for many years. However, possible changes of thermal properties of such liquids have not been in focus. The article presents an analysis of nanoparticle influence on thermal properties of mineral oil used in transformers. The investigated nanoparticles were fullerenes C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sub> and barium oxide TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The measured thermal properties were thermal conductivity, specific heat, viscosity, density, and the thermal expansion. On the basis of measurement results of the mentioned thermal properties, the authors calculated the heat transfer factor α. This factor determines the ability of a liquid to carry away heat and it has the key influence in transformer cooling. The measurements were done for a wide temperature range from 25 to 80°C.

articleTitle: Influences of frequency on space charge formation in polyethylene under high voltage AC electric fields
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Space charge behaviours are strongly linked to the electrical characteristics of dielectric materials. Large amounts of space charge in the insulation greatly contribute to the early aging and even electric breakdown. In general, the AC breakdown strength of an insulation is lower than that of DC breakdown strength. However, the limited results show that the amount of charge measured under AC condition is significantly lower than that under DC condition and depends strongly on the frequency of the applied voltage. Further investigation about the role of space charge in AC breakdown of the insulation is required. In this work the charge dynamics in low density polyethylene from low frequency (0.5 Hz) to power frequency (50 Hz) have been measured and analysed to reveal the influences of applied voltage frequency on space charge formation. Pulsed electro-acoustic method was used to detect the charge within the insulation, and twenty phase angles per cycle were recorded in order to illustrate the charge dynamics within each cycle. The results suggest the frequency of the applied fields can significantly affect the formation of space charge within the insulation. Using the subtraction technique, it has been found that a large amount of mobile charges exists under AC condition and the amount of charges decreases with increasing frequency. The relationship between charge dynamics and the AC breakdown strength of the material is explained.

articleTitle: Simulate the effect of trapped charges and trap cross-section on aging process
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The developed DC space-charge life model has been used to investigate the effect of trap cross-sections and trapped charges on the aging process in polymers. The experiment was performed using a two-dimensional grid that consists of multiple squares with micro dimensions that are treated as isolated regions. This grid was used to represent the evolution of damage structures during the aging process. Similar conditions to the experimental ones were applied to the simulations in terms of the applied fields and ambient temperature. During the aging process of both investigated parameters, most of the isolated regions at low electric field are damaged and consequently the damage path direction between the electrodes is significantly affected. At the end of the aging period, acceleration of the damage path increases rapidly with increasing electric field, in contrast to the low electric field. Based on the damaged regions, it was possible to extract a threshold field from the plot of electric field versus damaged regions during aging. The simulations undertaken by varying either of the parameters gave a different lifetime to the experimental results and this is supported by physical interpretations.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of epoxy composites containing both molecular and nanoparticulate silica
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Dielectric properties of epoxy composites containing both molecular and nanoparticulate silica were studied. The comparative dielectric study consisted in comparing neat epoxy and composites containing 1 wt% of nanosilica and both 1 wt% of nanosilica and G-POSS. After establishing the respective expected behavior of the basic composites, experiments have shown that the performance of the composite containing both additives was less performing than the composites containing solely 1% wt nanosilica or 1 wt% POSS. The use of two or more additives together has been often considered for attaining polymer multifunctionality and enhanced performance. In this framework, this work is a clear counterexample.

articleTitle: Investigations on ageing of low density polyethylene under polarity reversals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: To reverse the power flow, line commutated converter based HVDC transmission systems use polarity reversal. Insulation is an integral part of any power system, therefore it is of importance to analyze the performance of insulating material for better reliability and safety. The paper attempts to address the performance of insulation under polarity reversals and effect of these reversals on age/life of insulating material. The aim of the experiments is to study the ageing of low density polyethylene and to determine the value of power law coefficient of low density polyethylene under the effect of polarity reversals. The authors have conducted a series of experiments under accelerated thermal conditions to quantify the effect of number of reversals, voltage levels and time-step of application of polarities and to determine the ageing coefficient or the power law exponent ‘n’ under the given experimental conditions. The insulation selected for the experiments is low density polyethylene (LDPE), since it is believed that polymeric insulation is most susceptible to the effects of space charge formation. The voltage profile is in the form of square wave. The time-period and amplitude of the wave is varied to observe the effect on the number of polarity reversals occurred before breakdown of LDPE samples. The number of reversals are recorded and fitted in a statistical model to analyze the variation of voltage levels and time-gap between reversals. The number of polarity reversals was recorded before breakdown of LDPE samples at different voltage levels with different pulse duration. The value of power law coefficient is determined for different pulse duration. The discussion includes impact of dc ageing as well as reversals on the life characteristics.

articleTitle: Change in the electrical properties due to modification of the epoxy network structure using reactive diluents
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: There is a wide range of commercial applications that utilize epoxy resin as a main insulation material. Recent studies revealed that changing the molecular structure in epoxy/anhydride systems, by the introduction of a reactive diluent, can significantly improve the electrical properties. This research is of interest for high voltage applications, because the introduction of these reactive modifiers may provide a means of tailoring the dielectric properties of epoxy resins, such as permittivity and conductivity. The results reported in this work reveal that the addition of a reactive diluents greatly affects the glass transition temperature, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>, the permittivity, the DC conductivity and the breakdown strength. This can be explained through the reactive diluent leading to a significant modification of the epoxy network, whereby changed free volume caused by the presence of small branches alters the properties of the system. Therefore, the concept described, in principle, may be used to varying material properties in a controlled manner to tailor the properties of epoxy resins.

articleTitle: Characterization of solid-liquid interface for wet-mate subsea HVDC connectors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Wet-mate connectors are essential components in a submarine HVDC system. Solid-liquid insulation systems play an important role in the electrical insulation performance of a WM chamber. In this paper, the electric field distribution in synthetic ester oil of a solid-oil insulation system is studied by using Kerr electro-optic technique where the measurements were carried out with the presence of moisture and ionic contaminants. Moreover, effect of voltage polarity on the electric field distribution in the oil is investigated. For two solid liquid interface geometries studied, the electric field norm decreases gradually from the ground electrode to the HV electrode under positive DC while it remains almost constant for an applied negative DC voltage. The deviation of magnitudes of electric fields particularly near the electrodes suggests the presence of positive ions in the oil under positive and negative testing conditions.

articleTitle: High field dielectric properties of low density polyethylene with rough abrasive surface under AC ramp electric field application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Latest power cables which insulating material is cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) have taken measures to prevent water tree deterioration. Thus, not only its operating electric field, but also its stability and reliability are getting higher. However, due to operating for long duration, it is also considered that there is a risk of sudden breakdown from a very small defect or contaminant in the insulator. Therefore, it is very important to study the dielectric properties of LDPE with mechanical damage on film's surface under AC high field. To estimate the influences of mechanical damage on film surface to the high field dielectric properties, a simultaneous observation of dissipation current and EL has been carried out. The conduction mechanisms under ac high field have time dependence. Thus, it is very important to make the electric field application history equal in each sample. So a simultaneous observation under an AC ramp electric field application was introduced to control it. It makes simple to evaluate the time dominant phenomena under AC high field. In order to estimate the influences, five kinds of mechanically damaged LDPE films were prepared. From the results of the simultaneous observations of these samples, the influences of mechanical damage to the dielectric properties are discussed.

articleTitle: Thermal decomposition of cyclohexane by Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations and its relevance to streamer formation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo was used to simulate the decomposition of cyclohexane at temperatures up to 10 000 K. Rate constants needed for the simulations were obtained from literature and combined with differences in Gibbs free energy between the reactants and products. The degree of decomposition and an approximate heat capacity for cyclohexane were combined with finite element analysis to find the initial radius of a newly formed streamer channel. The initial channel was found to be of the order of 0.05-0.1 μm, expanding to a few μm after relaxation.

articleTitle: Effect of DC corona on performance of Pulsed electric field pretreatment on waste activated sludge
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: With the purpose of improving the efficiency of anaerobic digestion for waste activated sludge, μs-Pulsed electric field (μs-PEF) has been employed for pretreatment on waste activated sludge and its features of low energy consumption and high efficiency make it a promising method for industry application. In this work, DC corona has been used to assist the μs-PEF treatment on the sludge and the treatment efficiency has been estimated by measuring the soluble chemical oxygen demand, NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-N and total phosphorus. The influence of the polarity and magnitude of DC voltage on the treatment efficiency has been discussed. Obtained results showed that DC corona assisted PEF has higher treatment efficiency than PEF treatment. It is suggested that electroporation of microbial cell membrane within the sludge is likely to occur easily with the initial treatment of DC corona, which in turn facilitates the disruption of cell membrane.

articleTitle: Study of nonlinear nanoparticles doped silicone rubber composites and its dielectric properties
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: For the purpose of changing dielectric behavior of silicone rubber composites to obtain desirable dielectric properties, variety of inorganic particles fillers were doped into silicone rubber composites. In this paper we researched the dielectric properties of silicone rubber composites doped by nonlinear fillers, including zinc oxide(ZnO) with the size of 40nm and barium strontium titanate (BST) with the size of 200nm and measured the dielectric constant (ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>), dielectric loss angle tangent (tanδ) and resistivity(ρ). Various mass fractions (0%,10% and 24%) of nanosized nonlinear powder (BST and ZnO)are doped into silicone rubber to obtain multi-phase dielectric composites. The parameters were measured at room temperature and different electric field with the intensity increased from 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>V m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> V m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> was applied. The result showed that BST and ZnO fillers tended to exhibit enhanced dielectric constant and lower tan because of the increase of effective mass fraction. The influence mechanism were discussed in accordance with the mass fractions, electric intensity and polarization mode of each kind of nonlinear fillers.

articleTitle: Breakdown in air along insulating solid surfaces of different natures, parallel or perpendicular to the field direction
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: A study of creeping discharges in air under impulse voltage is presented. A large variety of insulating solids, either dry of wet, are investigated with two field geometries, parallel or perpendicular to the solid surface. Pre-breakdown streamers are investigated by high speed visualization and transient current measurements. Breakdown is primarily affected by the solid permittivity, whereas solid chemical nature and presence of water have a negligible influence. The influence of permittivity is larger in perpendicular field configuration, and very weak in parallel. In the latter case, the initiation and propagation of streamers are favored along the solid surface. However, streamers responsible for the transition to breakdown propagate above the surface. This provides an explanation for the small influence of the solid nature on breakdown voltage in parallel field.

articleTitle: Surface and breakdown resistance of polyethylene-based nano-dielectrics containing graphene-like additives
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this work, nanopowders of graphene oxide (GO) and functionalized graphene (G*) have been mixed with low-density polyethylene (LDPE) to fabricate samples with low filler weight ratio. A peculiar fabrication method was utilized, which consisted of ball-milling followed by thermal pressing. Electrical properties like resistance to erosion due to partial discharge (PD), and breakdown values were detected and the results were compared with those obtained on the neat LDPE. It is highlighted that the addition of G*, in particular, improves significantly both resistance to PD activity and the electric strength of LDPE specimens.

articleTitle: Partial discharge properties of resin molded insulation substrate after long term voltage application
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper deals with partial discharge (PD) properties of 0.32 mm thick Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> insulation substrate molded with epoxy resin after long term voltage application. Copper sheet electrode is attached on both sides of the ceramic substrate, which is used for insulation and heat dissipation in a power module. Two kinds of specimens are prepared having different partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV), namely, Sample H and Sample L with 10 and 6 kV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf>, respectively. As a result, it is found that PDIV of both specimens have not significantly changed, while applied voltage - charge (V-q) and PD occurrence phase - charge (ϕ-q) characteristics changed and the charge have decreased. The results of V-t characteristics assumed to be obeyed as V=Kt<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1/n</sup> provide estimation of minimum n value of 31. It follows that the lifetime of Si<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> substrate under voltage application of 1.2 kV<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rms</inf> is estimated to be more than 50 years.

articleTitle: Quantitative visualization of gas temperature distribution in atmospheric DC glow corona by spectral image processing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This study presents an experimental method of determining a two-dimensional image of the gas temperature in atmospheric DC glow corona by spectral imaging. A steady-state glow corona discharge as a partial discharge was generated by applying positive DC voltage to rod-to-plane electrode in synthetic air (N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:79%, O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:21%) at atmospheric pressure. Spectral imaging displays an image, and measures its specific spectra at each pixel in the image. The spectral images were taken by an Intensified CCD camera (ICCD) with ultra-narrow band-pass filters, corresponding to head and tail of nitrogen second positive system band (0-2) (2P(0-2)). The gas temperature was estimated from the emission intensity ratio between the head and tail of 2P(0-2). In this result, the change in the distribution of gas temperature in a positive DC glow discharge due to the amplitude of applied voltage was clearly visualized by spectral image processing.

articleTitle: Current-density vs electric-field intensity characteristics of polypropylene filled with natural clay as nanomaterial
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In this study, current-density vs electric-field intensity characteristics of polypropylene-based nanocomposite films are presented with concentrations of 0%, 2% and 6% nanosize natural clay by weight. Each nanocomposite sample is subjected to a 60-Hz, sinusoidal voltage waveform. During the experiments, applied rms voltage and current are recorded as the voltage increases across the test sample. The test was repeated with five samples with the same nanofiller content. The current-density vs electric-field intensity characteristics indicate a nonlinear behavior for each sample under consideration with some degree of saturation. From these characteristics, it was observed that the inception of saturation occurred at higher electric field intensities for the nanocomposites filled with natural clay than the unfilled polypropylene. The relative permittivity of of each sample was almost constant up to a critical electric field at which the saturation starts. Above that critical electric field, relative permittivity dramatically dropped.

articleTitle: Determination of transfer function of power transformer winding sections for partial discharge localization using design information
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The paper focuses on simulating the transfer function of power transformer winding sections based on design information. The calculation method has been investigated and discussed. The simulation of windings through multi conductor transmission line method has been performed for an actual distribution transformer in the laboratory using the design information. With this information the transfer function of the transformer winding sections has been calculated. Additionally some measurements on the distribution transformer have been done in three test platforms with different measurement devices in order to compare the methods for evaluating the transfer function of this transformer. The simulated transfer function has been adapted by comparison between the simulation and measurement results. As a result of the comparison, a deviation factor could be defined and the most sensitive parameters of the simulation methods could be identified. The difference between simulation and measurement leads to knowledge about the required measurements on a transformer as basis for the simulation of the transfer function of the transformer winding sections.

articleTitle: Wide-band model for dielectric response of oil-impregnated paper insulation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: To address the equivalent model of dielectric response of oil-impregnated paper insulation, the paper outlined a method to effectively determine parameters of the extended Debye model (EDM) using frequency domain spectroscopy (FDS) in wideband. Firstly, vector fitting method (VFM) was employed for rational approximation of the FDS curves. Thereafter, the capacitance and resistance in geometry and polarization branches of EDM were determined using circuit synthesis method. Further, to match clear physical essence in dielectric behaviors, passive enforcement was applied to strictly confine each component of EDM to be passive. In case study, a condenser body of an actual 126kV oil-impregnated paper condenser transformer bushing was modeled and solved using the proposed method. Comparative analysis on the reconstructed FDS, and RVM test results finally validated the effectiveness of the proposed method. The work conduces to improving the multi-parameter fitting problem of EDM parameterization using frequency response data.

articleTitle: Relaxor characteristics in interacting dipole systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the so called relaxor materials one finds unusual high susceptibilities and also in the Arrhenius plot of the relaxation times a nonlinear curve, often described as a Vogel-Fulcher law, instead of a straight line. These characteristics are modeled by systems of interacting charges which fluctuate thermally activated in intrinsically asymmetric double well potentials. Typical relaxor features are evoked by intrinsic asymmetries of the double well potentials due to heterogeneities in the material. To get the high susceptibilities of relaxors one has to take into account the electrostatic interaction between the charges. According to an approach of Pierre Weiss, this interaction is considered via a mean field proportional to the polarization itself. This field modifies the local fields at the double wells. Therefore the charge transition rates between the wells are influenced by the polarization: We get a feedback loop for the polarization. This feedback vastly increases the susceptibility.

articleTitle: UHF sensor for PD detection on wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The environmental matters fostered the power generation using renewable energies. This led, among the different possible solutions, to the diffusion of wind farms for wind power generation. The wind farms could be constituted by different kind of wind turbines with different kind of generators. Considering the nature of this generation systems, remote controlled diagnostic solutions should be implemented. A predictive maintenance program based on partial discharges (PD) measurements on the power generator and electrical apparatuses installed in the nacelle could be useful. In fact partial discharge measurements permit to obtain information on the insulation systems conditions. Preferably, not invasive PD sensors should be installed for continuous on line PD activity monitoring. In this view, radiated PD signals could be detected by means of UHF antennas. The measurement could be affected by the noise coming from electronic devices and sources transmitting in the same frequency band useful for PD signals detection. Therefore, a noise map has to be well defined to evaluate the best PD signal receiver bandwidth. Preliminary in site test campaigns have been performed in order to characterize an ad hoc UHF antenna designed for PD detection. The noise in the bandwidth of the considered antenna has been measured locating the sensor in different positions inside the nacelle. The acquired signals during the measurement campaigns have been post processed and analyzed. The preliminary acquisitions permitted to determine the amplitude and the frequency range of the noise in the different sites. The frequency ranges with low level noise have been identified and the preamplifier bandwidth was set coherently. This allowed to achieve a high signal-noise ratio.

articleTitle: Space charge modulated electrical breakdown of oil impregnated paper under AC-DC combined voltages in frequencies of 50∼600 Hz
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: High-frequency harmonics occur in converter transformers, which may lead to unexpected breakdown of oil impregnated paper insulation under ac-dc combined voltages with high frequencies. Here in this paper, the breakdown characteristics of oil impregnated paper insulation under ac-dc combined voltages in frequencies of 50~600 Hz were experimentally investigated. After considering the characteristics of charge injection, hopping and diffusion, the space charge behaviors in the ac-dc breakdown process were investigated based on a modified bipolar charge transport model. The results show that the breakdown voltage decreases with increasing ac offset ratio (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ac</sub>/(V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ac</sub>+V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dc</sub>)), and the breakdown voltage decreases with an increase in applied frequency regardless of the ac offset ratio. It is observed that homo-charges are accumulated during ac-dc breakdown, and the charge density in the vicinity of the electrodes increases with elevating applied frequency, leading to an enhancement of the built-in electric field distortion and thereby resulting in a decrease of the breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: AC breakdown strength of a natural ester transformer liquid under accelerated thermal ageing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In recent years, there is an increasing interest in applying natural esters as the alternative to mineral oils in large power transformers. But the low resistance to oxidation/gelling process poses a challenge for applying natural esters in free-breathing transformers. Some previous studies presented the gelling/oxidation behaviour of natural esters in terms of physical and chemical properties. There is a lack of study considering the electrical performance of natural ester during the gelling process. In this paper, the AC breakdown strength of a natural ester from liquid state to totally gelled state was determined. Test cells with a 1 mm sphere-sphere electrode gap were used to hold ester samples. The ester samples and the test cell were aged together in an air-circulating oven at 120 °C. Dynamic viscosity of the ester samples was also measured to monitor the oxidation/gelling process. Results showed that dynamic viscosity of the natural ester increases more than 100 times during the gelling process. But unlike the rapidly changing physical parameter, AC breakdown strength of the natural ester remains stable during the whole ageing process till the natural ester turns into totally gelled form.

articleTitle: Electric field behavior in mass impregnated HVDC cable insulation: Effect of cavity formation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This paper presents the effect of the presence of cavities on electric field behavior in mass impregnated (MI) HVDC cable insulation. Simulations have been carried out to investigate the influence of paper gaps and cavities therein. The effect of the conductivity of the gas medium inside the cavity is also studied. The simulation results show that the electric field is much lower in the paper gaps compared to the surrounding impregnated paper insulation. It is also observed that the presence of cavities increases the electric fields in the paper gap and surrounding insulation layers. The increase in electric fields due to the presence of cavities is highly dependent on the nature of the gas inside the cavity as well as the shape of the cavity.

articleTitle: Effects of nanoparticles on trap depth in epoxy resin under different temperature
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Under high DC voltage, the space charge accumulation can largely alters the local field distribution in epoxy resin. And it has been revealed that nanoparticles have great influences on space charge distribution in epoxy resin. To reveal the mechanism of nanoparticles, the effects of nanoparticles on trap depth are investigated under different temperature. In this work, epoxy resin and its nano composite are cured with a thickness of 0.3mm. The space charge distribution and the decay after the removal of voltage were tested based on Pulsed Electro-Acoustic (PEA) method under different temperature (20 °C, 40 °C and 60°C). The average charge density and trap depth are achieved by PEA. To eliminate the effects of temperature on decay rate, the trap depths under different temperature are calibrated to that of 20°C. The results indicated that the incorporation of nano silica particles could suppress the space charge accumulation in epoxy resin, and the nano composites show shallower trap depth than pure epoxy. Moreover, the trap depths of nano composites changes less obviously with the variation of temperature, while the trap depths of pure epoxy become deeper with the increase of temperature. This different trap behavior is explained in terms of the thermal movement of polymer molecules in epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Surface preparations on MV-sized cable ends for ramped DC breakdown studies
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The rising demand for HVDC crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) cable systems has put many novel products and solutions on the market within the recent years. In order to assess electrical performance of physical interfaces, DC breakdown studies of XLPE cable samples have been performed. For these samples, the surface of the XLPE in the cable ends has been modified using different techniques. Besides changing the surface preparation method, also the impact of the test conditions has been studied. A slowly ramped DC voltage has been used in order to study the breakdown characteristics for the samples. A great impact on breakdown voltage was found depending on which surface preparation was used. This highlights the fact that interfaces indeed play an important role for HVDC applications.

articleTitle: Liquids permeation into HTV silicone rubber under AC/DC electric field
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: As shed and sheath materials, high temperature vulcanization (HTV) silicone rubber suffers from various types of environmental stresses in actual use. Liquids permeation, as a kind of silicone rubber aging factor, has been investigated by many researchers. However, most of the studies are conducted under the condition of no electric field. Since that composite insulators, especially the high voltage (HV) side, are under high electric field, it is worthy of attention on liquids permeation under AC/DC voltages. In this study, we utilized a new-designed liquids permeation test unit under AC/DC electric field to measure the weight of HTV silicone rubber specimens during the test process. Deionized water, as well as basic fuchsine ethanol solutions were used to verify the effects of electric field on liquids permeation. Besides, the influence of ATH content on the liquids permeation was involved.

articleTitle: Control of leakage-current and power dissipation by surface texturing of silicone rubber insulators
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Partial arcing of external insulation in polluted environments is substantially reduced for composite structures with polymeric housings compared with ceramic insulators and bushings. However, loss of surface hydrophobicity combined with heavy deposits of saline or other conductive compounds negate this advantage and risk tracking or erosion. It is shown that mitigation of this risk is provided by moulded surface textures that increase the form factor and effective creepage distance of the insulation. Inclined-plane and fog testing are used to quantify the reduction of leakage-current and power dissipation.

articleTitle: Zeolite nanoparticles: A new generation of nano-dopant for nanodielectrics with high electrical strength
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: It has been concluded that the enhanced electrical properties of nanocomposite dielectrics (nanodielectrics) are mainly contributed by the phase interface regions which are attributed to the large specific surface area of the nanoparticles. This research introduces zeolite nanoparticles as the nano-fillers with microporous structures to obtain more phase interface regions and further improve the electrical strength of the PP/zeolite nanodielectrics. DC breakdown tests indicated that zeolite particles of specific pore size can improve the breakdown strength by very low doping concentration (about 0.1 wt.%). Thermally stimulated current (TSC) tests demonstrated the decreased intrinsic deep traps and introduction of new deeper traps which can be attributed to the large amount of phase interface regions introduced by zeolites.

articleTitle: Linear particles behavior caused by circuit breaker action in GIS
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The linear metallic particles which are static lying on the GIS enclosure have less harmful to the insulating property. However, the insulating property will reduce in a large degree when the metallic particles once stand and beat in the GIS cavity. Many papers have discussed the behavior of linear particle in the GIS affected by the type and shape of the particles, the pressure of the gas insulation, and the electric field, however, very little research has been conducted on the behavior of linear particles under the mechanical impact caused by the operation of circuit breaker. In this study, an impact vibration test platform is built to investigate the deterioration of the gas dielectric strength in a 126kV prototype proportion shrinking GIS. A high speed camera is applied to record the movement behavior of the particle. The experiments are repeated with different size of linear particles. The deterioration of the dielectric strength under different voltage are discussed, and the movement characteristics are presented. The results indicate that: the impact force reduces the lift voltage of linear particles, e.g. the lift voltage of a particle with 15mm length and 0.3mm radius decreased from 36kV to 25kV. Secondly, the lift voltage drop ratio decreased with the size of the particles under the same impact force. Finally, movement characteristics of linear particles after lifting are different, the particle rotates and bounces between conductor and GIS tank without impact force, apart from that, the particle may stand on the shell after lifting with impact force.

articleTitle: On the effects of molecular composition, morphology and ageing on the electrical properties of polyethylene
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polyethylene is widely used as the basis for the insulation in high voltage cables, commonly, in the form of cross linked low density polyethylene (XLPE). With time, the chemical and electrical properties of the pristine polymer begin to change, depending on the molecular architecture, morphology and ageing processes. In this work, thermal treatment, based on accelerated ageing in air was performed on the exposed surface of polyethylene blend films (HDPE/LDPE) at temperatures above the melting point for various treatment times. The ageing degrees were quantified by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, while dielectric spectroscopy was used to investigate the dielectric response. Space charge dynamics were measured using the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) technique. It was found that the dielectric loss after long treatment times was significantly increased, corresponding with the carbonyl index. Furthermore, space charge results show that homocharge was increased at short treatment time; however, it is noticeable that, after long treatment times, charge injection appeared to be affected by surface oxidation and, in this way ageing has a marked effect on the electrical behaviour of the blend.

articleTitle: PD characteristics of metallic protrusions in SF6-insulated coaxial electrode arrangements at DC stress
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Metallic needle protrusions were investigated experimentally on the ground side of a commercial coaxial GIS duct regarding their PD characteristics in time domain. DC voltages of up to 400 kV were applied to the SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>-insulated arrangement at pressures in the range of 100 … 500 kPa. Specimen of needles featured tip radii in the range of micrometers; protrusion length was in the range of few millimeters. PD measurements were performed using three different measurement principles in addition with voltage measurement simultaneously. Orientational measurements were performed during voltage rising test to approximately twice the inception voltage. Constant voltage measurements were performed at 10% and 20% above the determined discharge inception voltage.

articleTitle: Stochastic character modelling of breakdown under lightning impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The breakdown process under lightning impulse voltage is still not fundamentally investigated. As noted in previous studies, for a given lightning impulse voltage in an air gap, it is very difficult to predict whether a breakdown occurs or not. Additionally, in case of breakdown, the time to breakdown is stochastically distributed. This paper presents a method to model the stochastic character of breakdown under lightning impulse voltage. In order to apply the methodology, several measurements on an air gap (rod-rod electrode configuration with a length of 3 m) under lightning impulse voltages with different crest values have been carried out. Therefore, the probability of breakdown and also the probability density of the time to breakdown are calculated. The probability density of the time to breakdown is approximated by the Weibull distribution function. The parameters of Weibull distribution function are derived in dependence of the voltage crest value using the maximum Likelihood method. Accordingly, a Monte-Carlo simulation can be performed in order to reproduce the stochastic character of the breakdown. It will be shown that the stochastic character of breakdown under lightning impulse voltage can be probabilistically modeled. For this purpose, the probability of breakdown and the needed time to breakdown can be estimated by normal and Weibull distribution functions, respectively. The validity of the proposed model will be proved by comparing the simulation and measurement results. A synthetically reproduction of a data set of the breakdown test, which has a similar statistical pattern as measurement results, can be taken out from this study.

articleTitle: Partial discharges of nonwoven nanofibers composite
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: A promising technology of nanofibrous composites is studied nowadays as an alternative method to the well-known dielectric nanocomposites filled by various nanofillers like a metallic oxides, alumina, silica, carbon nanofibers or nanotubes. All of these nanofillers are known, more or less. The use is to improve some of the electrical, mechanical and thermal properties of nanocomposites. Unfortunately, its expensiveness and tendency to agglomeration remain as their main disadvantage. In the contrary, the nanofibers can be applied as a nonwoven fabric over the surface of the composite with no tendency to create the cluster agglomeration as the nanocomposites with nanoparticles. It was prepared experimental specimens of nonwoven nanofibers composites based on the modification of commonly used three-component mica-based electrical insulating material (epoxy, glass fibers and mica). The modification of these, well known, mica composites was done by incorporation of the nonwoven nanofibers layers (1, 2 and 3) to its structure always with different area density (1, 3 and 5 g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of the nanofibers. The tested material was delivered in the form of resin-rich sheets on which the layers of the nanofibers made from Polyamide 6 were applied and specimens were subsequently cured using typical resin rich curing process. The influence of prepared modifications on the partial discharge characteristics and magnitudes of the resulting nanocomposites was studied. Partial discharges results show differences between the specimens' variations depending on nanofibers presence, the number of layers and surface density of nanofibers. The decreasing of the partial discharge activity is recognisable when the nanofabrics is incorporated into the composite. The obtained results proved that the nonwoven nanofibers based on Polyamide 6 seem to be a perspective material with certain resistance to partial discharge activity.

articleTitle: Low-density polyethylene/polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes composites obtained by extrusion
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Low density polyethylene/polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxanes (LDPE/POSS) composites were fabricated by melt blending with a twin-screw extruder under a rotation speed of 200 rpm and barrel zone temperatures of 115-130 °C. Two types of POSS were investigated: octamethyl POSS (OmPOSS) and isooctyl POSS (IoPOSS). Microscopic features of the samples were observed by scanning electron microscopy to evaluate the effectiveness of extrusion in producing nanodielectrics. In addition, dielectric properties of the samples were characterized by broadband dielectric spectroscopy, progressive-stress breakdown tests and surface partial discharge tests. The results showed that extrusion was effective in producing LDPE/OmPOSS and LDPE/IoPOSS micro-composites. Moreover, both composites had a low dielectric permittivity at 50-60 Hz. Furthermore, the erosion resistance of LDPE/IoPOSS saw an improvement of 45% without compromising its breakdown strength whereas LDPE/OmPOSS increased its erosion resistance by 23% at the cost of a reduced breakdown strength.

articleTitle: On the arc-resistance when tested with DC- and AC-stress by the example of silicone elastomers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The paper provides results of investigations with the high voltage arc test with AC and DC voltage in a step test similar to IEC 61621. Tests at DC with a constant current provide typically a lower withstand time than tests at AC which is in line with results from Inclined-Plane-Tests. Depending on the insulation material the arc-test withstand time in the DC-step-test can be lower or equivalent to those at AC stress. It is found that the arc shows a rather high mobility at the cathode at low current. Increasing current leads to lower mobility of the arc. IR temperature measurement under AC and DC stress shows significant higher temperatures at DC in comparison to AC. In comparison to the test at AC there seems to be an intensification of the stress at higher levels of the test current under DC-stress. The insulating material itself seems to affect the mobility of the arc and thus the test results. Further a comparison of high voltage arc and Inclined-Plane-Test results are carried out.
