Aside from the noticeable improvement in the breakdown strength, the Weibull modulus of the laminate was substantially increased with coating, over a wide temperature range. The permittivity of the laminate was influences by the existence of an interface and the loss was maintained as low as that of the pristine glass.

articleTitle: Open-circuit thermally stimulated currents in LDPE/Al2O3 nanocomposite
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Polyethylene doped with nanoparticles of inorganic oxides has been studied extensively during the last decade, aiming at its possible use as suitable material in insulation of high voltage direct current cables. To elucidate electrical properties of such material, thermally stimulated discharge (TSD) currents are analyzed in samples of low-density polyethylene (LDPE) filled with Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanoparticles and compared with the response of pure LDPE. The latter exhibits a presence of two peaks in the TSD spectrum, which yield levels of activation energies close to earlier published data. For LDPE nanocomposite, a single broad peak is found instead, which when decomposed into a number of single peaks yields higher and broadly spreading activation energies. This indicates a presence of deep traps in the nanocomposite and explains significant reduction of its DC conductivity and strong suppression of space charge accumulation, as compared with unfilled LDPE.

articleTitle: Investigation on hydrophobicity transfer property of silicone rubber under heavy contamination
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Silicone rubber (SIR) suffer from high contamination when insulators operate in heavy industrial area, thus further research about hydrophobicity transfer property under heavy contamination is needed. In this paper, NaCl was used as soluble salt and industrial kaolin was used as inert material to study hydrophobicity transfer property of room temperature vulcanized (RTV) SIR and high temperature vulcanized (HTV) SIR. Both RTV and HTV specimens were deposited with contaminant of different SDD, NSDD and different special contaminant composition. By continuously measuring static contact angle for 600h, the influence of SIR material, SDD, NSDD and contaminant composition to hydrophobicity transfer were compared and discussed. The measurement shows that RTV has much better hydrophobicity transfer behavior than the HTV. High SDD would result to crystalize of the salt on the surface, but it has no evident effect on the hydrophobicity transfer. High NSDD would slow down the hydrophobicity transfer speed, but its influence decrease over time. Different contaminant composition has significant influence to the hydrophobicity transfer process, reflected by different transfer speed and static contact angle at the steady state. ZnO, chemically pure kaolin and kieselguhr have much better hydrophobicity transfer behavior than industrial kaolin and Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. Experiment with heavy contamination and 600h's hydrophobicity transfer shows that SIR and contaminant composition are the decisive factor to the hydrophobicity transfer. However, the relationship between contaminant com and hydrophobicity transfer needs further investigation.

articleTitle: 60 years in the research on electron energy distribution functions: Future challenges
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Electron energy distribution functions occupy a central role in the theoretical and numerical analyses of interaction of electrons with neutral species in the general area of gas discharges. The input parameters for the calculation of energy distribution functions are the various collision cross sections as a function of electron energy, over a wide range, a few milli-eV up to 100 eV. The output parameters are the transport properties and swarm coefficients as a function of the reduced electrical field. In this paper the progress that has been achieved over a period of 60 years - a period of author's personal involvement - has been critically examined. A simplified method for calculation of the average properties of the electron swarm has been developed and shown to yield very good results in xenon. Future challenges in the light of expanding applications of plasma science are discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of influencing factors of Dissolved Gas in oil
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: As an important means of insulation testing, Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) in oil reflect the insulation condition of transformer. However, a lot of factors influence the dissolved gas of transformer. Some of them should be taken into consideration during the analysis, especially when it comes to the typical gas concentration. In this paper, an evaluate method of influencing factors is proposed. With this method, the effect degree of influence is quantified and the typical gas concentration could be modified. Firstly, collect and process the DGA data, removing invalid data and filling missing data. Then, classify DGA data according to each influence factor. With the different classification, each cluster center can be figure out by K-means. Calculate the average Euclidean distance of cluster centers as the influence evaluating indicator. Each kind of classification corresponding to a Euclidean distance value, regard the Euclidean distance value as the influence level. The further distance means the greater influence. Finally, classify the data according to the influencing factor and calculate the typical value with the statistic method. As an example, DGA data from two grid has been collected and tested. It comes to a conclusion that voltage grade, operation years, oil type have much stronger influence than the installation location. According to the conclusion, the classification of DGA has been done and typical gas concentration which corresponds to voltage grade, operation years, oil type has been calculated. The field test shows that, with the modified typical gas concentration, the defect was identified correctly, which means the great value of this method.

articleTitle: Electrical and dielectric properties of Mn-doped ZnO varistors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: ZnO varistors have been extensively used against transient surges because of the excellent nonlinearity. ZnO varistors are obtained by sintering semiconducting ZnO powder with small amount of metal oxide additives. Amongst, Mn-doping is effective in the enhancement of the nonlinearity. In this paper, the relationship between the microstructure, the electrical and dielectric properties of Mn-doping ZnO-Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> based varistors is investigated. The results show that with the increase of Mn-doping content, the grain growth is facilitated. Both the extrinsic and intrinsic defect relaxations can be adjusted by Mn additives. Mn-doping can improve the height of double Schottky barriers by enlarging the interface-state density of the depletion layer in the grain boundary. But too much Mn-doping can improve the concentration of intrinsic defects, resulting in the decrease of the barrier height.

articleTitle: Study on space charge behaviors and trap characteristics in LDPE/SiO2 under thermal aging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Space charge is a threat to cable insulation materials and polythene insulation gradually degrades in long service conditions. The degradation of low density polyethylene (LDPE) affects space charge formation, accumulation and dissipation, and the presence of space charge affects the performance of dielectric. This paper focuses on the space charge characteristics of LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites under thermal aging. The SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles were added into LDPE matrix with single mass concentration 5wt%, and the LDPE and LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> samples were aged at a hot spot temperature (90 °C). During thermal aging, the space charge distribution was measured at a regular interval (0, 10, 20, and 30 days) at room temperature. And the pulse electro-acoustic (PEA) method was used for space charge measurement. It was suggested that SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nano-fillers increased the density and depth of traps in LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanocomposites, and the LDPE/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> samples had a certain anti-thermal aging ability at the initial aging stage. In addition, thermal aging changed the microstructure of LDPE materials, produced many chemical defects, and also increased the density and depth of traps. Generally, long term thermal aging had significant influence on the space charge behaviors of polyethylene materials, and appropriately filling SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanoparticles could delay the degradation of LDPE insulation materials.

articleTitle: The transition of surface charge during partial discharge sequences under low pressure
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The homogenous discharges under low pressure have been widely used in many fields, but the influence factors that determine the discharge characteristics are still not clear. So, it is necessary to study the formation mechanism of homogenous discharge and transition process from partial discharge to homogeneous filamentary discharge. It was known that residual surface charge on the dielectrics play an important role to the discharge characteristics as it greatly affects the electrical field distribution in the discharge gap. In this paper, a surface charge measurement system based on Pockels effect was established to investigate the surface charges distribution under different gas pressure, and the influence of the surface charge on the discharge features was discussed together with the discharge current and statistical spectrum. Moreover, the simultaneous discharge phenomenon was experimentally studied. It was found that the number of simultaneous discharge and the discharge probability within several cycles were both important factors on the transition from partial discharge to homogenous discharge under low pressure.

articleTitle: Punctured rubber bladders detected by UV-vis spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: For the design of power transformers, two mechanical solutions are used to hinder the contact of the oil with the outside atmosphere. One method favoured in the United States is to seal the transformer using a nitrogen cushion. The other method is to use an elastic rubber or plastic bag to separate the surface of the oil from the gas space in the conservator. Under service conditions, rubber bladder may be punctured due to aging or mechanical problems such as gasket wear, with potential oxygen inlet. Such problems need to be detected to avoid dramatic failures. In this contribution, three 500 kV generator step-up units belonging to Salto Grande were sealed and a periodic oil analysis procedure implemented to monitor the rubber bladers. Measuring the interfacial tension and the acidity of the oil, confirmed the lack of oxidation products while the analysis of the relative content of Dissolved Decay Products (DDP) in the oil by UV-vis spectrophotometry (ASTM D6802) showed a higher content of dissolved oxidation decay products in the units with punctured rubber by bladders.

articleTitle: Effect of corrosive sulfide deposition on thermal conductivity of insulating paper
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: As transformer accidents occur frequently, one of the main reason for such accidents has been confirmed after the disassemble researches with the deterioration of oil-paper insulation caused by the existence of corrosive sulfide. Taking this situation into consideration, a volume of researches have been undertaken in this paper to understand the effect of different dibenzyl disulfide (DBDS) concentration on the formation of corrosive products and its influence on paper insulation, in sulfur corrosion experiments for 3 days at 150 °C temperature, according to the IEC 62535 standard. It turns out that in the process of experiments, corrosive sulfur which slowly deposits on the surface of the insulating paper, causes the decline of both the coefficient of thermal conductivity and thermal capacity of insulating paper. As a result of it, local overheating will accelerate sulfur corrosion and enhance the deposition on the surface of the insulating paper, conversely leading to the degradation of thermal conductivity and thermal capacity of insulating paper.

articleTitle: The influence of mass moisture invading on electrical features for oil-impregnated paper bushing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Oil-impregnated paper bushing (OIP) is one of the key devices for power transformers. Recently, some explosion accidents were initiated by bushing invaded by mass moisture, which could destroy the power transformer. In order to study the influence of mass moisture on the characteristics of dielectric loss (tanδ), capacitance and partial discharge (PD) of OIP, a 25kV transparent glass-bushing model was designed and ultrasonic humidifier conducted moisture invading. After moisture invading one-hour and stewing 12 hours, the online measurements of tanδ, capacitance and PD were used for OIP model under applied AC voltage of 10kV, 15kV, 20kV, 25kV and 30kV separately. The results show that tanδ increased from 0.62% to 0.72% under the AC voltage of 10kV and the increase of its magnitude under the voltage from 10kV to 30kV was 33.88%. The capacitance increased from 102.6pF to 103.8pF under the AC voltage of 10kV and the increase of its magnitude under the voltage from 10kV to 30kV was about 0.28%. The PD character was almost unchanged under the voltage from 10kV to 30kV. It is indicated that the change of dielectric loss tanδ is much higher than the PD character for OIP under mass moisture invading. Therefore, the online monitoring of dielectric loss tanδ should be reconsidered and expended to detect the serious moisture defect of OIP. It is applicable to the condition monitoring of moisture of bushings. It may provide reference for the condition monitoring and maintenance of OIP for the operation of the power system.

articleTitle: Research on the measurement of electric field in liquid dielectric under lightning impulse voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The insulating performance of the liquid dielectric plays an important role in the operation of the transformer. It has been verified by numbers of fault cases occurred in the release testing on transformers, that flashovers and breakdowns of insulating pressboard occurred in the angle rings, shielding rings and outlet device frequently, while an impulse routine test was processing. Study on the distribution of space electric field in the liquid dielectric under the impulse voltage is helpful to optimize the design of insulation structures, with rich theoretical and engineering value. The ex post fault analyses are usually based on a simulation result instead of experimental measurement. Kerr effect method is a non-contact online electro-optical measurement on the electric field in liquid dielectric. We established a rapid measuring system consisting of optical system, test cavity, impulse power supply and photo-detector, the whole system calibrated in propylene carbonate with a high Kerr constant. The calibration result indicates that the measuring system has a fine response rate and the deviation between the measured electric field and the applied electric field is less than 3.65%.

articleTitle: Modeling of charge transport in nanodielectrics using a coupled finite element and Monte Carlo approach
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: This work presents an innovative approach to modeling the charge transport in dielectric polymers and their nanocomposites by coupling finite element analysis (FEA) with the Monte Carlo (MC) simulation. The stochastic charge hopping among localized states can be well captured by the MC simulation. The altered electric field distribution due to nanofillers can be computed by FEA and contributes to the energy landscape of the localized states. The modeling faithfully reproduces the transient and dispersive nature of the transport as exhibited in many experiment measurements. With nanofillers as deep traps, the modeling also demonstrates the importance of the filler morphology to the effectiveness of charge trapping.

articleTitle: Space charge properties of PPLP insulation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: The space charge accumulation in the lapped dielectric has been a concern as it may affect the reliability of the insulation. This study intends to investigate charge dynamics in the polypropylene and in the lapped sample with Kraft paper, with or without the impregnating oil. The space charge profiles were tested using the pulsed electroacoustic technique (PEA) under same DC electric field. Both ionization and charge injection have been found in Kraft paper. For the lapped samples, significant amount of charge has been found accumulated at the interface that has the same polarity as the nearby electrode.

articleTitle: Influence of water absorption on space charge behavior of epoxy nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Nowadays a large number of researches have been focused on properties of epoxy based nanocomposites with an intention to create materials with enhanced properties. Literature review shows space charge behavior in dielectric materials will strongly affect the electrical performance and presence of moisture will influence space charge characteristics. In the present work, owing to the well-known water absorption of epoxy system, the “volts-on” PEA measurement has been used to measure space charge behavior in epoxy and its nanocomposites filled with nano-SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and nano BN in both dry and undried samples. Thus, an overall picture of the influence of water absorption on space charge characteristics in epoxy nanocomposites can be obtained. In addition, the DC conductivity measurement will be processed to further understand the charge mobility in undried samples.

articleTitle: Influence of the ambient gas on the charging efficiency of tubular-channel fluoroethylenepropylene (FEP) copolymer ferroelectrets
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: Ferroelectrets (also called piezoelectrets) are non-polar polymer foams or polymer systems with internally charged cavities. The charging process represents a series of dielectric barrier discharges (DBDs), and is critical for the piezoelectric properties of ferroelectrets. DBD charging relies on the breakdown of the gas molecules, and therefore strongly depends on the gas components inside the cavities. In this paper, we study the influence of gases with lower (helium) and with higher (nitrogen or air) breakdown strength on the charging efficiency of tubular-channel fluoroethylenepropylene (FEP) ferroelectrets. It is found that filling the cavities with helium results in low threshold voltage, facilitating the DBD charging process. However, a lower threshold voltage leads to a lower value for the remanent polarization because back discharges occur at lower charge level when the charging voltage is turned off. Via gas exchange involving helium and nitrogen during charging, the charging efficiency of tubular-channel FEP ferroelectrets can be significantly enhanced.

articleTitle: Interface matters in dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE Conference on Electrical Insulation and Dielectric Phenomena (CEIDP)
abstract: In the dielectric and electrical insulation research field, phenomena at interfaces between different substances are important issues. To promote innovative research activities, especially in industries, collaborations among researchers with different types of expertise are essential. An application engineer of measurement systems can work as an interface of different research fields and contribute to interdisciplinary activities, as well as the measurement technologies themselves.
